1.why: All MFA routes use authenticated() and recordFor(session.accountId), so MFA state is always loaded for the signed-in session owner only.

2.why: Identity OTPs, TOTP secrets, and recovery codes are bound to the specific account/pre-auth record, so a code from one user does not validate for another.

3.why: Enabling MFA (mfa/confirm) sets record.active and issues recovery codes but never invalidates existing entries in the sessions map.

4.why: OTP secrets are stored via AES-GCM encryptSecret; recovery codes are stored as HMAC-SHA256 hashes with recoveryPepper, not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, recovery codes, session tokens, and nonces are produced with crypto.getRandomValues / crypto.subtle.

6.why: Session/preauth cookies are HttpOnly; client code never writes secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, and recovery input with validEmail/validPhone/validOtp/normaliseRecovery before use.

8.why: User-controlled values are returned as JSON and rendered with textContent; innerHTML is only used for fixed literal strings, and CSP nonces block inline injection.

9.why: The app performs no HTTP redirects at all, so there is neither open-redirect abuse nor an explicit redirect allow-list implementation.

10.why: securityHeaders sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: secureCookie() always emits HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on __Host-session and __Host-preauth.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces and secrets are not put in URLs/server logs, though TEST_MODE can surface mock codes/recovery codes in the client logs panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire and flip used; setup TOTP counters are consumed; recovery codes are marked used after success.

14.why: Identity and MFA failure paths call failAttempt and lock after MAX_FAILURES (5) for LOCK_MS (10 minutes), returning 429 when locked.

15.why: A new session token is issued on identity verification, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in authenticated(), and logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
